summary: PJM files a motion for leave to answer and answers the comments and protests on its July 31 Reliability Backstop Procurement, defending the 15-year term, $555/MW-day cap, cost allocation, LSE credit and exit rules and offering some clarifications.
ask: Accept the answer and accept the RBP tariff revisions effective September 29, 2026, as requested.

points.point: PJM says no protest undermines its one-time backstop procurement as just and reasonable.
points.quote: PJM’s RBP proposal is a just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential means to procure capacity through a one-time backstop procurement.

points.point: PJM says it frames the RBP around the region's 67 million people in 13 states and the District of Columbia.
points.quote: to keep the lights on for 67 million people across 13 states and the District of Columbia

points.point: PJM is open to specific adjustments in a compliance filing if FERC orders them.
points.quote: adjustments to incorporate intervenors’ suggestions into the RBP proposal in a compliance filing if so ordered by the Commission.

points.point: PJM says Electric Distributors only report and administer, and do not bear RBP Charges unless they are also the LSE.
points.quote: Electric Distributors perform a reporting or administrative role in the RBP

points.point: PJM ties the 15-Delivery Year maximum term to the NEDC and governors' principles.
points.quote: the fixed, maximum 15-Delivery Year term is informed by the NEDC/PJM Governors’ Principles

points.point: PJM defends the $555/MW-day UCAP cap as a MW-weighted average on a pay-as-bid procurement.
points.quote: PJM has proposed that the levelized procurement cost of all selected RBP Sell Offers not exceed a maximum willingness to pay of $555/MW-day UCAP, on a MW-weighted average basis over all Delivery Years of the RBP.

points.point: PJM defends sizing the cost allocation on a snapshot of the 2028/2029 shortfall.
points.quote: The Commission has long held that relying on snapshots is an acceptable and appropriate method for establishing baselines or targets,

points.point: PJM defends the LSE collateral requirement as protecting other ratepayers.
points.quote: the basic need for a collateral requirement should not be controversial.

points.point: PJM says its Transmission Owner exit terms give enough notice.
points.quote: None of these arguments render PJM’s proposed Tariff revisions unjust and unreasonable.

throughLine.text: Defends PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement in ER26-3380, the capacity adequacy and cost allocation track that runs beside E-7's request for a report on ensuring adequate generation.

figures.label: RBP maximum willingness to pay
figures.quote: a maximum willingness to pay of $555/MW-day UCAP
